summary.tldr: Creates a new commissioner to monitor and investigate Canadian business conduct abroad and report on compliance with international human rights law.
what_it_does: Creates the Office of the Commissioner for Responsible Business Conduct Abroad and gives the commissioner a five-year term, staff, and deputy head powers.
Applies to Canadian entities that operate abroad, import goods made abroad, provide services abroad, or control those entities.
Lets any person complain about the international human rights impact of an entity’s business activities abroad, and lets complainants ask for their identity to stay secret.
Authorizes the commissioner to investigate on a complaint or on their own initiative, if there are reasonable grounds to think an entity may not respect international human rights law.

Requires the commissioner to publish reports with findings and may recommend compensation, apologies, policy changes, and federal steps such as withdrawing trade advocacy support or Export Development Canada support.

Creates offences for obstructing an investigation or giving false or misleading information, with fines of up to $250,000; also requires annual reports, special reports, and a five-year parliamentary review.
summary.background: The bill would replace the current Canadian Ombudsperson for Responsible Enterprise role with a new commissioner. The person holding that office when the change starts would stay in office until the end of their term.
